title: dinostomp findings feed
description: The machine-readable form of FINDINGS.md. FINDINGS.md is the source of truth; this file is generated from it by scripts/index_findings.py and validated against this schema before it is written. Compatibility: within a major version, fields are only ADDED. Removing a field, renaming one, or changing its type is a major bump.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS contract, not of dinostomp. Check the major before parsing.

tool.description: Which battery produced these findings. `engine` is the SHA-256 of dinostomp's own code and schema pack, the same value recorded as tool_sha256 in every run manifest.

status_classes.description: The closed vocabulary status_class draws from, with what each one means. Published in the feed so a consumer never has to guess at a bucket.

id.description: Permanent. A withdrawn finding keeps its id and says what killed it, so ids are never reused and never renumbered.

subject.description: What the finding is against: a dataset, a harness, or dinostomp itself.

check_label.description: Verbatim prose, e.g. "`dup-options` (S5)" or "the data-scope battery". Not every finding comes from one named check; use `checks` for the machine-readable ids.

checks.description: MAY BE EMPTY, and often is: roughly a third of these entries are findings about the battery, a loader or a method rather than the output of one check. An empty list means no check id was claimed, never that the check is unknown.

date.description: VERBATIM from the ledger, and NOT guaranteed to be a date. One entry reads "first live fleet" because that is what it was dated against. Parse `date_iso` instead.

date_iso.description: Null whenever the ledger did not carry a full day, which includes every month-only and free-text date. Null is not missing data; it is the ledger declining to claim a precision it does not have.

status.description: Verbatim, including qualifiers and inline links: "confirmed, underpowered", "fixed in v0.50.0".

status_class.description: A LOSSY bucket derived from the leading word of `status`. The qualifiers are dropped, so a `confirmed` here may be scoped, marginal or underpowered in the ledger. Read `status` before quoting one.

url.description: Permalink into FINDINGS.md on the default branch, so it tracks the current text of the entry rather than the version you fetched.
